subject: Access controls & support access follow-up (RBAC, break-glass, logging)
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.inference>
To: Sam Reynolds <sam.reynolds@fintrust.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.inference>
Date: 2026-10-01T15:12:00-07:00
Subject: Access controls & support access follow-up (RBAC, break-glass, logging)

Hi Sam —

Thanks for taking the time today. Quick recap from our discovery focused on data handling and access controls:

- PII & data residency: FinTrust will keep production data in us-east-1 and needs confirmation that logs/keys are not replicated outside the region.
- Retention & logging: You need 90-day access logs for audit and an exportable logging feed for your SIEM.
- RBAC & least-privilege: Role-based access with segmented roles (admin, engineering, readonly, support) and scoped permissions per environment.
- Support access / break-glass: Temporary support access with MFA, time-limited sessions, and recorded justification/audit trail.

Next steps we discussed:
1) I'll share our SOC2 evidence index and a short RBAC diagram.
2) Vivek can run through a technical runbook for break-glass and session recording.
3) If helpful, we can prep an example MFA + SSO flow for your SAML IdP (Okta).

Can you confirm:
- the list of FinTrust roles you expect (or a sample mapping)?
- whether legal needs a copy of the SOC2 evidence or just a summary?

Attaching: security questionnaire (blank copy) so you can mark responses and return.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.inference | +1 (415) 555-0147

Attachments:
- FinTrust_security_questionnaire_v1.pdf

From: Sam Reynolds <sam.reynolds@fintrust.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.inference>
Cc: Alicia Gomez <alicia.gomez@fintrust.com>, legal@fintrust.com
Date: 2026-10-02T09:08:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Access controls & support access follow-up (RBAC, break-glass, logging)

Thanks Marissa — good summary. A few notes and answers from our side:

- Roles: we'll start with three roles for the pilot: admin (limited to infra ops), dev (model/endpoint deploys), and support_readonly. We may add a compliance role later.
- Residency: confirmed — production data must remain in us-east-1 and logs must be able to be stored in our AWS account or exported to our SIEM.
- Logging: 90 days is a hard requirement right now. Need a way to export audit logs (S3 or syslog).
- Support access: we need break-glass that requires a ticket number, two approvers, and an audit record that can't be altered.

Attaching our completed questionnaire and a short checklist of legal asks. Could you also share:
- an example RBAC policy or diagram for how Redwood maps roles to API permissions, and
- detail on how support access is requested/approved and how session activity is recorded?

We'd like to schedule a 30-min technical follow-up with Vivek next week (Tue/Wed preferred).

Thanks,
Sam Reynolds
Head of IT Security | FinTrust
sam.reynolds@fintrust.com

Attachments:
- FinTrust_completed_questionnaire.pdf
- fintrust_legal_checklist.docx

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.inference>
To: Sam Reynolds <sam.reynolds@fintrust.com>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.inference>, Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.inference>
Date: 2026-10-02T11:40:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Access controls & support access follow-up (RBAC, break-glass, logging)

Appreciate the quick turnaround, Sam — received the questionnaire and checklist. A few items to call out (high level):

RBAC / least-privilege:
- Redwood supports fine-grained role mapping. Typical roles we surface: organization_operator, deployment_engineer, model_admin, billing_readonly, support_readonly.
- Policies are enforced at the API/route level and at the UI. We can provide a mapping doc that translates your three pilot roles to our permission set.

Support access / break-glass:
- Break-glass flow: support engineer requests access via support portal -> request requires ticket number + justification -> request auto-notifies two approvers (configurable) -> access granted for a configurable time window (default 2 hours).
- All break-glass sessions are logged with: requester identity, approver identities, start/end timestamps, and a session recording link (if session interacts with customer data). Recordings and logs are immutable (WORM) for the configured retention period.

Logging & retention:
- Audit logs are exportable to your S3 or syslog. We retain logs for customer-configured retention (can be set to 90 days).
- Access logs, admin actions, and model prompts (if configured) are all available for export. We can redact PII at ingestion if required.

Next steps / proposed plan:
1) Vivek — could you prepare a short RBAC diagram (map the three FinTrust roles to Redwood permission sets) and a one-page break-glass runbook to circulate?
2) We'll upload SOC2 evidence index and RBAC diagram to a shared drive and send a link.
3) Schedule a 30-min technical call next Tue/Wed (cc'd Vivek).

Proposed times (PDT): Tue 10/6 10:00-10:30, Tue 10/6 15:00-15:30, Wed 10/7 09:00-09:30. What works best?

Best,
Marissa

--
